proposed_edit.prior_line: Changing variable t=1/u in the convergent integral yields I(s)=-lambda I(2-s). Thus the sign in the completed functional equation is -lambda. The separately established equality of the elliptic L-function with L(f,s) identifies this sign with w(E). Consequently w(E)=-product_(p^e||N)w_(p^e), as used at main15181.
proposed_edit.replacement_line: Changing variable t=1/u in the convergent integral yields I(s)=-lambda I(2-s), so the newform sign is -lambda. To compare it with the elliptic sign, use Atkin–Lehner Theorem3, p147, with k=1: at p|N the primitive newform coefficient a_p is0 if p^2|N and is±1 otherwise, with local factor (1-a_p p^(-s))^(-1). Silverman C.16, p449, gives elliptic bad factors (1-b_p p^(-s))^(-1) with b_p in{0,1,-1}. Equality of all good factors gives D_E(s)L(E,s)=D_f(s)L(f,s), where D_E and D_f are the respective finite products of these bad-factor denominators. Analytic continuation preserves this equality. Both products are holomorphic and nonzero at1, since each factor is1 or1±1/p. Thus the two L-series have the same central order r. The completion factors are nonzero at1, and the functional equation gives sign(-1)^r by its first nonzero Taylor coefficient. Silverman TheoremC.16.3, p451, supplies the elliptic functional equation. Hence w(E)=-lambda=-product_(p^e||N)w_(p^e), as used at main15181. The actual associated-form trace domain p not dividing2N covers every good prime because the separately checked minimal-discriminant argument gives2|N. No equality of the two full L-series or their special values is asserted.
proposed_edit.scope: Replace the unused full-L-equality premise by a proved equality of central orders from nonzero finite Euler-factor ratios. Preserve all other lines.

use.reason: The actual E_l is a nonsingular elliptic curve over Q with conductor N; the theorem's explicit curve quantifier applies. Take the theorem's associated form, with its stated integral Fourier coefficients and trivial nebentypus. The trace comparison ranges over q not dividing 2N. Shimura needs eigenform status at all operators, not trace comparison at all primes. The p.1007 normalized convention and the p.1010 Euler series with constant term one identify the association's a_1=1. No rescaling is inferred from prime traces. The same f, level N, and integer coefficients enter both subsequent cards. Normalized Fourier T_q gives a_q as eigenvalue by its n=1 coefficient. At level primes use the U_p coefficient rule, not a good-prime Euler factor. Good trace comparison uses the actual reductions of E_l. Since v_2(Delta)=8 for odd l and model change alters it by multiples of 12, 2 divides N for this curve. No equality at excluded primes is extracted. The theorem-heading attribution does not change the stated hypothesis. Shimura gets a common normalized eigenform with coefficient field Q; Faltings gets the stated comparison only outside a finite set.
